explanation: Variable declaration in C is the process of specifying the type and name of a variable to the compiler, which allocates memory for it. It is used to ensure proper data handling, prevent errors from undefined variables, and maintain code readability and type safety in programs.
code_example: int myVar;  // Declaring an integer variable
myVar = 10;  // Assigning a value to the variable
example_explanation: This example declares an integer variable named myVar, assigns it the value 10, and prints it using printf. It demonstrates how variable declaration reserves memory and allows the variable to be used in the program, showing the basic workflow from declaration to usage.

merged_from.source: The C Programming Language - Kernighan & Ritchie
